preamble: Fortition of the palatal glide [j] to a voiceless postalveolar affricate [tʃ]. The clearest case is word-initial Proto-Turkic *y- (*j-), which became voiceless [tʃ] (Cyrillic ч) in the Yenisei and Sayan Turkic languages of South Siberia (Khakas, Shor, Tuvan), where Kipchak languages have voiced [ʒ]/[dʒ] (Kazakh, Kyrgyz жер) and Oghuz keeps [j] (Turkish yer). The change is regional; the far more common fortition outcome of *j is voiced [dʒ] (cf. Latin iam > Italian già [dʒa], which belongs in j_glide_to_j_affricate). In Paikoneka (Arawakan, Bolivia) the palatal glide *j fortited to ʧ and merged with the inherited affricate.

examples.note: Initial *y- > [tʃ]; Khakas ⟨ч⟩ is the voiceless postalveolar affricate.
Proto-Baure-Paikoneka *j and *ʧ merged as ʧ in Paikoneka; Baure keeps j.
